title: Initiative Thermostat: capacity-slit and convergence protocol for company OKR oscillation
creator: Arielle Gomez
description: Problem: Company-level objectives oscillate between squads each quarter, causing duplicate work, burst capacity overruns in Dedicated, and unclear escalation paths. Goal: Design an operational 'initiative thermostat' — a protocol and lightweight tooling to slice initiative capacity, converge strategic threads, and surface automatic guardrails that prevent cross-team oscillation while preserving speed. Scope: cross-functional alignment protocol, a capacity-slit template for initiative intake, an SLA mapping model to translate OKR targets into reserved throughput/points, and a cockpit view in the Console roadmap map. Out of scope: implementing enforcement in infra (this ticket delivers the spec, acceptance criteria, and pilot plan).
acceptance_criteria: A public playbook published in Confluence that describes the initiative thermostat protocol and step-by-step intake flow
Capacity-slit template (.csv/.xlsx) that maps OKR target lines to engineering commit units and Dedicated capacity buckets
Decision matrix that ties initiative priority, risk, and customer impact to a recommended SLA tier
Pilot run with two cross-functional initiatives (Search Latency and Console Rollouts) and documented learnings
Roadmap cockpit mock in Figma and a Console dashboard spec for capacity burn / cross-team conflicts
success_metrics: Reduction in duplicated initiative work across teams by 40% in pilot quarter
Decrease burst over-commit incidents in Dedicated by 30% for pilot initiatives
Time-to-decision for initiative intake reduced from 8 days to 2 days (measured in pilot)
>80% of stakeholders rate the thermostat protocol as 'useful' or 'very useful' in post-pilot survey
tasks: Draft protocol doc and intake checklist
Create capacity-slit template and populate with example historical data
Work with Eng to create SLA translation model (points -> throughput/GPU hours)
Design cockpit UI prototype with Design (Figma) and Console product owner
Run pilot with two initiatives and collect telemetry and stakeholder feedback
Produce a retrospective and recommended rollout plan for company-wide adoption

notes_decisions: Decision 2026-03-04: Pilot will use 'soft enforcement' (alerts + manual gating) to avoid disrupting live SLAs.
Decision 2026-03-09: Capacity-slit will be defined as a triple (committed engineering points, Dedicated GPU hours, slack buffer percentage).
Trade-off: stricter enforcement reduces oscillation but increases ticket friction; chosen approach balances with a clear escalation runway.
